items.title: 13.8.2 Reaction of silver halides (AgX) with aqueous ammonia

blocks.text: Adding aqueous ammonia tests the solubility of the silver halide precipitates. AgF is soluble in water and gives no precipitate, so ammonia has no effect. The white precipitate of silver chloride dissolves in dilute ammonia to give a colourless solution of the diamminesilver(I) complex: AgCl(s) + 2NH3(aq) gives [Ag(NH3)2]+(aq) + Cl-(aq). The cream precipitate of silver bromide dissolves in concentrated ammonia, also giving a colourless solution: AgBr(s) + 2NH3(aq) gives [Ag(NH3)2]+ + Br-. The yellow precipitate of silver iodide does not dissolve in dilute or concentrated ammonia, so there is no change. Table 13.6 summarises the sequence.
